newsitem.title: UK: Europe funds buy equities, sell bonds in Feb - poll.
newsitem.headline: Europe funds buy equities, sell bonds in Feb - poll.

text.p: Fund managers in continental Europe are bullish on prospects for equities in their region, with bulls outnumbering bears by 60 percent on a one-year view, Merrill Lynch said in a survey released on Monday.
The survey also said the managers were buyers of equities in continental Europe in February, outnumbering sellers by 34 percent.
It said fund managers in the region were still not keen on European bond markets.
It noted a marked improvement in sentiment towards French equities and away from German equities.
They said fund managers in the region expect stronger European economies for the coming year and are bullish on prospects for corporate profits.
There were fewer sellers of U.S. equities among continental European managers in February. They were neutral on UK equities, turned buyers of Japan and were keen on Pacific Basin equities.
They were no longer raising cash allocation and were sellers of bonds inside and out of the region.
Among fund managers in other regions, UK managers were raising their European exposure, U.S. manangers were less interested in Europe, and Japanese managers were keen buyers.
The survey was carried out by Gallup on behalf of Merrill Lynch in early February, covering 68 institutions.
